parsed.headline: Advance voter turnout increases for Toronto's 2026 municipal election

pages.text: Advance voting for Toronto's 2026 municipal election saw 222,550 eligible voters participate during a six-day period that ended on October 11, 2026, at 7 p.m. According to CBC Toronto, this represents the largest advance voter turnout in over a decade and a nearly 72 per cent increase compared to the 129,000 early votes recorded during the 2023 mayoral byelection. Election day is scheduled for October 26, 2026. On that day, eligible voters must cast ballots at their assigned voting places as indicated on their Voter Information Card or the Toronto Elections webpage. Voters who requested to vote by mail were required to return completed packages to Toronto Elections by noon on October 14, 2026. To meet this deadline, voters were advised to use one of 25 secure, indoor yellow Toronto Elections Mail-in Voting drop boxes located in each ward across the city. These boxes are monitored by CCTV, inspected regularly, and emptied daily by Elections staff. Voters can verify if a Mail-In Voting package was received on time using a confirmation code. Additionally, registration for third party advertisers, which includes any person, corporation, or trade union intending to spend money to promote, support, or oppose a candidate, closed at 4:30 p.m. on October 9, 2026. Registrations were to be filed in person at the Toronto Elections City Hall office at 100 Queen St. W., first floor, Permit Alley.

A recent survey from Liaison Strategies conducted during the advance voting period suggests incumbent Mayor Olivia Chow leads the mayoral race by five points, polling at 51 per cent among decided and leaning voters. Councillor Brad Bradford is polling at 46 per cent. In response to the turnout and polling, Chow’s team credited the results to the efforts of volunteers campaigning across the city to encourage supporters to vote. Conversely, Laryssa Waler, a spokesperson for Bradford’s campaign, stated that the high early turnout indicates voters are not waiting until October 26 to make up their minds.

parsed.headline: Prayer vigil held in Waterford for four family members killed in arson attack

pages.text: Hundreds of people attended a prayer vigil at the Sacred Heart Church on Wednesday for four members of the English family who died following an arson attack in Waterford. The service included prayers, songs, and memories of the deceased. Kim English, Philip English, and two of their children, nine-year-old Jayden and 12-year-old Callum, died after their home on Birch Avenue was set on fire on October 13, 2026. It is believed an incendiary device, likely a petrol bomb, started the fire while six members of the family were sleeping. Two children were severely injured in the blaze and remain in critical condition at a Dublin hospital. Alex O'Sullivan, a coach at Johnville FC, described Callum as a fantastic player and a lovely child. Gardaí (Irish police) described the investigation into the murders as intense and very active. On the evening of October 13, 2026, police conducted multiple searches and seized vehicles and electronic devices for technical examination.

parsed.headline: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman conducts meetings during first UN General Assembly visit in New York

pages.text: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman leveraged his first visit to the United Nations General Assembly in New York to showcase the country's potential and present his national plans, according to Irene Khan, Bangladesh’s permanent representative to the UN. Speaking to The Daily Star, Khan stated that Rahman attended the high-level event from a Monday evening until a Friday evening, conducting approximately 30 meetings within that four-day window. These engagements included 10 meetings with UN agencies, one regarding the Rohingya issue, two focused on climate change, and a major meeting with investors. Khan described the visit as a successful debut for the relatively newly elected Prime Minister, noting that delegations were eager to understand his vision and the direction of Bangladesh.

During the visit, Rahman communicated a message that Bangladesh seeks international cooperation and is willing to work with all parties without being beholden to any. Khan noted that Rahman emphasized the country is open for business and seeking investment, specifically highlighting plans for investment in social development and the upskilling of women and youth. Khan characterized the reception of the Prime Minister as a warm welcome, occurring at a time when she observed powerful states challenging international consensus and the UN.

parsed.headline: Three road security personnel killed in Hama countryside, Syria

pages.text: Three road security personnel were killed on Tuesday during an attack by unidentified gunmen in the Hama countryside of central Syria, according to the North Press Agency. A security source told Syria’s Al-Ikhbariya TV that security forces have been mobilized to investigate the incident and pursue those involved. At the time of publication, the Internal Security Forces had not issued an official statement regarding the attack.

parsed.headline: Bangladesh parliamentary committee discusses Ganges Water Sharing Treaty

pages.text: A parliamentary standing committee on the Ministry of Water Resources in Bangladesh discussed the nation's interests regarding the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty during its second meeting at the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban. Chaired by Mohammad Shafiqul Haque Milon, MP, the committee discussed whether the existing treaty would be renewed or continue, though a press release indicated that no final decision has been taken and the relevant process is ongoing. The committee expressed hope that the Padma Barrage project could be inaugurated in February 2027 and discussed a proposed inspection of the project site in Sujanagar upazila of Pabna district on October 25.

parsed.headline: Attack on Aramco building in Dhahran, Saudi Arabia sparks limited fire

pages.text: An administrative building belonging to the oil company Saudi Aramco in Dhahran, Saudi Arabia, was struck on the evening of October 13, 2026, resulting in a limited fire but no casualties or fatalities, according to a Saudi energy ministry official. Separately, the Saudi civil defence agency reported on Wednesday that debris from two intercepted Houthi missiles wounded four people and damaged 15 homes in the capital, Riyadh. Witnesses in Riyadh reported seeing projectiles and hearing explosions on Wednesday, following a phone alert stating the city was facing a hostile aerial threat. This follows an October 10, 2026, strike on Riyadh's international airport that killed 13 people and suspended operations. Following these events, U.S. President Donald Trump stated on Truth Social on October 13, 2026, that the Houthis are “behaving very badly,” alleging they are acting “probably at the behest of Iran” to drive up oil prices. Trump noted he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the group.

In response to the attacks, the Saudi-led coalition struck oil sites in Yemen on October 13, 2026, including a Yemen Petroleum Company facility on the outskirts of Sana'a. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki stated on X that the strikes targeted facilities in Sana'a and the western provinces of Dhamar and Saada used to supply the Houthi war effort. Houthi political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti stated the campaign against Saudi targets was intended to message Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman that he cannot wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position, adding that the group would target American interests if the U.S. intervened. The Saudi cabinet, led by the Crown Prince, vowed on October 13, 2026, that it would not allow its security or freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb Strait to be threatened. Meanwhile, the World Health Organization reported on October 13, 2026, that suspected cholera cases in Yemen had tripled in three weeks.
